questions.problem:
The level curves of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{3}y-{y}^{2}x$ are given by $f(x,y)=c.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. $c=-1$ gives a line

II. $c=0$ gives a parabola and the axes $x=0$ and $y=0$

III. $c=1$ gives two lines
questions.worked_solution:
Setting $f(x,y)=c$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{3}y-{y}^{2}x & =c \\ xy({x}^{2}-y) & =c\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

- If $c=\pm 1$ then the level curves are $xy({x}^{2}-y)=\pm 1,$ which are not lines.

- If $c=0$ then the level curves are $xy({x}^{2}-y)=0,$ which consists of the axes $x=0$ and $y=0$, and the parabola $y={x}^{2}.$

So, only statement II is true.

questions.problem:
The level curves of the function $f(x,y)=\sqrt{{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}}$ are given by $f(x,y)=c.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. $c=1$ gives a line

II. $c=2$ gives a hyperbola

III. $c=0$ gives two lines
questions.worked_solution:
Setting $f(x,y)=c$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}} & =c \\ {x}^{2}-2{y}^{2} & ={c}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore:

- If $c=1$ then the level curve is ${x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}=1,$ which is not a line.

- If $c=2$ then the level curve is ${x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}=4,$ which is a hyperbola.

- If $c=0$ then the level curve is $y=\pm \frac{x}{\sqrt{2}},$ which consists of two lines.

So, only statements II and III are true.

questions.problem: Which of the following represents the level curves of $f(x,y)=3\operatorname{sin}⁡x?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the range of $f(x,y)$ is $[-3,3].$ So, we will consider only $c$-level curves for $c\in [-3,3].$

The level curves for the function $f(x,y)$ are given by the equations 

$$
f(x,y)=c
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =c \\ 3\operatorname{sin}⁡x & =c \\ x & =\operatorname{arcsin}⁡\frac{c}{3}+2\pi n,\end{aligned}
$$

where $n$ can be any integer. 

Notice that the equations $x=\operatorname{arcsin}⁡\frac{c}{3}+2\pi n$ do not depend on $y.$ So, for a given $c\in [-3,3]$ and integer $n$, the right-hand side of the equation is constant. As a result, we obtain a family of vertical lines, as shown below.

questions.problem: Which of the following represents the level curves of $f(x,y)=2x+y?$
questions.worked_solution:
The level curves for the function $f(x,y)$ are given by the equations 

$$
f(x,y)=c.
$$

Notice that the range of $f(x,y)$ is $(-\infty ,\infty ).$ So, we will consider level curves for any value of $c.$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =c \\ 2x+y & =c \\ y & =-2x+c.\end{aligned}
$$

The equation above gives us a family of lines with slope of $-2.$ Therefore, the correct graph is as follows:

First, notice that the range of $f(x,y)$ is $[-1,1].$ So, we will consider only $c$-level curves for $c\in [-1,1].$

The level curves for the function $f(x,y)$ are given by the equations 

$$
f(x,y)=c.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =c \\ -\operatorname{sin}⁡y & =c \\ y & =-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡c+2\pi n,\end{aligned}
$$

where $n$ can be any integer. 

Notice that the equations $y=-\operatorname{arcsin}⁡c+2\pi n$ do not depend on $x.$ So, for a given $c\in [-1,1]$ and integer $n$, the right-hand side of the equation is constant. As a result, we obtain a family of horizontal lines, as shown below.
